documents.title: Orthopedics & Sports Medicine Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
New patient consultation, date of visit 12/09/2025

Re: Hui Huang, DOB 08/11/1997

Dear Doctor,

We saw Ms. Huang at your request for a swelling of the left wrist.

She noticed a soft bump on the dorsum of the left wrist roughly three months ago. It has never hurt. She finds it gets bigger and easier to see when she bends the wrist forward, and it varies in size from week to week. There was no injury. She has had no weakness or numbness in the hand.

Past history: none. Surgeries: none. Medications: none. Allergies: no known drug allergies. Family history: noncontributory. Social: software developer, never smoker, alcohol socially, one or two drinks a month.

Examination of the left wrist: a 2 cm, round, firm, mobile mass sits on the dorsal surface. It transilluminates with a penlight. The skin over it is unremarkable. Wrist motion is full. Motor, sensory and vascular examination of the hand is normal.

Impression: dorsal ganglion cyst, left wrist.

Plan: We reviewed what a ganglion is and that it is benign. Many shrink or settle on their own, so we agreed on a period of observation. She will come back in about three months, or sooner if it becomes painful or she has numbness. Treatment options can be revisited then.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in her care.

Orthopedics & Sports Medicine

documents.title: Orthopedics & Sports Medicine Follow-up and Procedure
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Follow-up visit and procedure note, date of visit 03/09/2026

Re: Hui Huang, DOB 08/11/1997

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Huang returned three months after her first visit with us for the left wrist ganglion. Over the six months she has had it, the lump has slowly enlarged. It stands out more after long stretches of typing. Any discomfort is minimal; what bothers her is how it looks. No injury in the interval. Medications: none. Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam: on the dorsal left wrist there is a 2 cm, round, rubbery nodule. It moves freely and is not tethered to deeper structures. The skin is intact without redness. It transilluminates. Wrist motion is unrestricted and strength is preserved.

Assessment: dorsal ganglion cyst, left wrist, unchanged in size, cosmetically bothersome.

We talked through continued observation, needle aspiration and surgical excision. She preferred to try aspiration today.

Procedure: aspiration of left dorsal wrist ganglion. Verbal and written consent obtained. Skin prepped sterilely; local anesthetic with lidocaine. Using a large-bore needle, approximately 1 mL of thick, clear, gelatinous fluid was withdrawn. The mass was no longer palpable afterward. Compressive dressing applied. No complications. Fluid not sent.

Plan: keep the dressing on for a couple of days. We explained that ganglia commonly come back after aspiration; if it recurs and still bothers her, excision is the next option. Follow up with us as needed.

Thank you for sending her to us.

Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
